content_sections.heading: About IISER Bhopal
content_sections.text: The Indian Institute of Science Education and Research Bhopal is on Bhopal Bypass Road, Bhauri, Bhopal 462066, Madhya Pradesh. This post is in its Department of Chemical Engineering. The fellow will work in the research group of Dr. Paramita Das, Assistant Professor, on a project funded by the SERB, DST, New Delhi, Government of India.

content_sections.heading: Project and Nature of the Position
content_sections.text: The project is called "Metal-Organic-Framework-based Electrochemical Sensors Incorporated on a Paper Scaffold for the Detection of Heavy Metal Ions in Water". It is open to Indian nationals. The notice describes the job as a Project-JRF. It runs "for 1 month or till the completion of the project". The notice also says this project-JRF position can be converted into an institute-funded PhD in the 2026-27 December cycle. FREEJOBALERT DAILY QUIZ Preparing for Govt Exams? content_sections.heading: IISER Bhopal JRF Eligibility 2026
content_sections.text: Candidates should be below 28 years old. B.Tech. and M.Tech. in Polymer Science and Engineering / Chemical Engineering / Materials Science and Engineering / Chemical Technology, or B.Sc. (Hons) and M.Sc. degree in Chemistry, from a recognized University/Institute. Minimum 60% marks or a CGPA of 7.5 and above on a scale of 10. A pass in a national-level examination such as GATE/CSIR-JRF/NET(JRF)/UGC-JRF/Rajiv Gandhi Fellowship, or any other equivalent fellowship, in Engineering Sciences/Chemical Engineering/Chemistry/Chemical Sciences/allied areas. Prior knowledge of Electrochemistry and some experience in electrochemical analysis and in designing materials for sensing applications (the notice says these candidates are "highly preferred"). Subject knowledge in electrochemistry and some experience with electrochemical characterization techniques, e.g., CV, EIS, stripping voltammetry and DPV. Mathematics as a subsidiary subject at the 12th and bachelor's level. Good analytical skills, some experience with characterization techniques such as SEM, UV-Vis and XRD, experiment design, handling of sophisticated equipment, and good English writing skills. Check the official notification for the full eligibility conditions of the post.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: Applications are shortlisted first. Only shortlisted applicants will be told and called for an interview. The institute will not reply to other messages while selection is going on, and it will not pay TA/DA for attending.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for IISER Bhopal JRF Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Put the full application into ONE single PDF file. Include a cover letter with a detailed CV and photograph. Give the names of two referees. Attach copies of all your credentials, including mark sheets from the 12th standard onwards and your NET/GATE qualification certificates. Email the PDF to [email protected] with the subject line "JRF Application for ANRF SPG project". Make sure the email arrives on or before 3 November 2026. Incomplete applications will be rejected without review. Send applications to: Dr. Paramita Das, Assistant Professor, Department of Chemical Engineering, Office 307, Academic Building -4, Indian Institute of Science Education and Research (IISER) Bhopal, Bhopal Bypass Road, Bhauri, Bhopal 462066.

faq.question: Q1. What will the IISER Bhopal JRF work on?
faq.answer: The fellow will work on metal-organic-framework-based electrochemical sensors built on a paper scaffold for detecting heavy metal ions in water. The project is funded by SERB, DST, under Project No. SERB/CHE/2023-2024/39.

faq.question: Q2. Can I apply without NET or GATE?
faq.answer: Yes. A national exam qualification is preferred, not required. Without CSIR/UGC NET or GATE, the pay is Rs. 30,000 plus HRA (as applicable) per month, or as per the funding agency's guidelines.

faq.question: Q3. What minimum marks do I need?
faq.answer: You need at least 60% marks or a CGPA of 7.5 and above on a scale of 10, along with the required B.Tech. and M.Tech. or B.Sc. (Hons) and M.Sc. degrees.

faq.question: Q4. Can M.Sc. Chemistry graduates apply?
faq.answer: Yes, if they also hold a B.Sc. (Hons) and their degrees are from a recognized University/Institute.

faq.question: Q5. Can this position lead to a PhD?
faq.answer: Yes. The notice says the project-JRF position can be converted into an institute-funded PhD in the 2026-27 December cycle.

faq.question: Q6. What subject line should the email have?
faq.answer: Use the subject "JRF Application for ANRF SPG project".

faq.question: Q7. Which documents go into the application PDF?
faq.answer: A cover letter with a detailed CV and photograph, the names of two referees, and copies of all credentials, including mark sheets from the 12th standard and your NET/GATE certificates.

faq.question: Q8. Which lab techniques will help my application?
faq.answer: The notice lists electrochemical techniques such as CV, EIS, stripping voltammetry and DPV, plus characterization methods such as SEM, UV-Vis and XRD.

faq.question: Q9. When would the selected candidate have to join?
faq.answer: The selected candidate is expected to join on or before 12 November 2026.

faq.question: Q10. Will I be paid travel costs for the interview?
faq.answer: No. The notice states that no TA/DA will be given to candidates called for the interview.
